# Orion

Orion is the constellation that is easiest to find in winter: three stars in a row form the belt, with the bright red Betelgeuse above and blue-white Rigel below. Below the belt hangs the Orion Nebula, a cloud of gas where new stars are born, visible as a faint smudge even to the naked eye on a dark night.

The nebula is a good first target for a small telescope, see [[Astronomy/telescope-setup]].
